chapter_plans.title: The Sunken Graveyard
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway arrives at the moorland graveyard, touches her first stone, and begins to lose the feeling in her fingers while meeting the evasive Arthur Penhaligon.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway arrives by taxi at the edge of the moor, carrying her kit. The graveyard is sunken, the ground uneven, and a single raven sits on the tallest stone. Arthur Penhaligon waits near the gate, gloved, watches her without greeting. He leads her to the central stone and sets a three-week deadline. Marget Halloway begins work, cleaning the first headstone. When she places her bare fingers on the stone, she feels a cold deeper than the temperature — and a faint vibration, as if something beneath is breathing. She pulls away, but the cold lingers. She records the sensation in her ledger, noting that her right index finger feels slightly numb.
must_happen: Marget Halloway arrives at the graveyard and observes the raven on the central stone (C006).
Marget Halloway meets Arthur Penhaligon, who is gloved and sets a three-week deadline.
Marget Halloway touches her first stone and experiences the persistent cold vibration (C001 planted as physical clue).
Marget Halloway records the first nerve numbness in her ledger.
must_not: No explanation of the cold or the raven is given by any character in dialogue.
No romantic or familiar interaction of any kind between Marget Halloway and Arthur Penhaligon.
chapter_plans.opens_with: The raven did not move when Marget Halloway stepped out of the taxi.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: She looked at her right index finger, pressed it against her own cheek — and felt nothing.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The raven never once turned its head, as if it had been carved from the same slate as the stone it sat on.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: A creeping unease in her chest as the numbness begins — the first time she cannot feel her own body.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write a 1600-1800 word chapter establishing the setting, characters, and first clue. The numbness track must begin with the cold in the fingers. Introduce the raven as a static presence. Arthur Penhaligon's gloves and evasiveness should create distrust. End with the cliffhanger of face numbness.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Marget Halloway's curiosity about the cold stone and Arthur Penhaligon's unexplained three-week deadline.

chapter_plans.title: Moss That Grows in Darkness
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway discovers the moss she cleaned has regrown overnight, and Arthur Penhaligon dismisses her concerns while she maps the cold spots and loses sensation in her thumb.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway arrives next morning to find the graveyard covered in fresh moss, thicker than before. The stone she cleaned is already veined with green. She marks the locations of the coldest spots, noticing the raven moves between them. Arthur Penhaligon arrives, pressures her to quicken the removal, dismissing the regrowth as 'the damp.' Marget Halloway records the second episode of numbness, now affecting her thumb. She begins to suspect the moss is not ordinary. The cold vibration from the first stone clings to her fingers longer yesterday — she confirms it is not ambient temperature but something intrinsic to the stone.
must_happen: Marget Halloway confirms the moss has regrown overnight despite her cleaning (moss regrowth established).
Marget Halloway begins marking cold spots with flags and observes the raven perching where the cold is strongest (raven on cold spots).

chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The raven shifted one step sideways on the stone, but its feet made no sound at all — like claws on slate muffled by something soft.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: The stubborn dread of being trapped in a job that feels wrong, and the first time she wonders whether Arthur Penhaligon knows more than he says.

chapter_plans.title: The Knife's Edge
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway tests the moss by scraping it and watches it regrow instantly, plants a behavioral clue about the moss's reaction, and feels the numbness spread to her palm.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: On the third day, Marget Halloway arrives determined to test the moss. She scrapes a patch from an older stone and watches it regrow within minutes — too fast for any natural lichen. Arthur Penhaligon finds her mapping the cold spots, reiterates the three-week deadline, and warns her not to 'touch the wrong stones.' The raven remains fixed on the central stone. That evening, reviewing her ledger, Marget Halloway notices the numbness has spread from her fingertips into her palm. She decides to ignore Arthur Penhaligon's instructions and investigate the central stone at dawn.

chapter_plans.title: The Stone That Breathes
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway touches the central stone at dawn and feels a rhythm beneath the cold, but Arthur Penhaligon confronts her and she loses sensation in her wrist.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway arrives at the graveyard before sunrise, determined to investigate the central stone. She places her palm on the stone and feels a slow pulse, like a heartbeat from deep underground. She marks the cold spots she has mapped and deduces they form a circle around the central stone—a pattern too deliberate to be natural (C002 planted). While tracing the stone's base, her fingers catch on a rough patch: an embedded shard of bone carved with a date that matches Oswin's disappearance (C010 planted). Arthur Penhaligon finds her there, his voice tight, orders her to stay away from the central stone or leave the job. Marget Halloway refuses, pointing out the pattern, but Arthur Penhaligon dismisses it as coincidence and walks away. That evening, she records in her ledger that the numbness has spread to her entire right wrist. She can no longer feel the pen she holds.

chapter_plans.title: The Circle Underfoot
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway tests her deduction by examining the center of the cold circle, finding a buried slate and a document that points to a hidden record of the graveyard's caretakers.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: At dawn, Marget Halloway returns to the graveyard with the pattern mapped in her head. She locates the geometric center of the cold spots—a patch of ground six feet behind the central stone that the raven never visits. She scrapes away the moss and finds a slate slab engraved with the words 'Root of Barrow'. Beneath it, tucked into a crack, she discovers a yellowed piece of paper listing names and dates of men who served as 'Keepers of the Stone' (C004 document planted). She uses the pattern to confirm her earlier deduction: the cold is not a natural phenomenon but part of a deliberate system (C002 payoff). On her way back, she encounters Arthur Penhaligon emerging from the moor, his shoes wet for the first time. He asks her if she has been 'digging' and his tone is cold. She denies it, but knows he senses something. That evening she records numbness traveling up her right forearm. The motion of writing has become clumsy.

chapter_plans.title: The Notebook Under the Stone
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway uses the keepers' document to locate Oswin Kerrow's hidden notebook, reads his detailed observations of the moss, and plants a physical clue that connects the raven to his fate.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway studies the keepers' document by lamplight and notices marginal notes in Oswin Kerrow's handwriting—a reference to a 'cache beneath the fifth stone'. She returns to the graveyard and, after counting from the central stone, locates a weathered headstone marked with a faint scratch. Beneath it she finds a tin containing Oswin Kerrow's notebook. The notebook records fourteen months of obsessive soil and moss observations: the cold's intensity, the regrowth speed, the raven's movements. On the final page, she finds a pressed feather and a scribbled line: 'I will take the root so the Barrow does not starve. The raven will remember.' (C004 payoff). She slips the feather into her own ledger (C007 physical planted). Arthur Penhaligon appears, his gloves stained with soil, and demands she hand over any documents she has found. She gives him a blank page from her cold-map ledger, but he takes the entire ledger, leaving her with only the hidden notebook. That night, she records numbness in her right elbow: her entire arm is now dead.

chapter_plans.title: The Drowned Plot
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Arthur Penhaligon confiscates Marget Halloway's cold-map ledger and deliberately floods the lower graves after noticing which stones she marked.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: The confrontation begun over Marget Halloway's ledger ends with Arthur Penhaligon wrenching it from her numb right hand and carrying it away. Marget Halloway follows him at a distance and sees Arthur Penhaligon open an old iron sluice above the lower plot. Water pours through only the row of graves she marked as having the strongest cold outside the central circle, burying the stones and their connecting seams beneath black runoff. Arthur Penhaligon watches until the final marker disappears, then leaves without examining the damage. Marget Halloway recognizes the timing as suspicious but cannot yet prove intent. She rescues one torn, waterlogged corner of her map from a drainage grate and hides Oswin Kerrow's notebook elsewhere. During the recovery, she tests her left hand and records the first numbness in two fingertips, while her entire right arm remains insensible.

chapter_plans.title: The Feather Points Down
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway proves Arthur Penhaligon flooded the graves to conceal the cold network, uses Oswin Kerrow's pressed feather to locate its center, and begins an experiment showing the moss remains connected underground.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway returns before Arthur Penhaligon can drain the lower plot and lays the torn map corner beside the surviving waterline. The flooded graves align exactly with her strongest cold marks, paying off C005 and establishing Arthur Penhaligon's act as targeted concealment. Marget Halloway removes the pressed feather from Oswin Kerrow's notebook and places it on dry slate beside samples taken from the flooded row. Frost forms along only one side of the feather, while the other remains limp; when she rotates the slate, the frozen vane continues to orient toward the central stone. The physical response pays off C007 without conveying language and confirms that the cold has a fixed center. Marget Halloway then seals moss samples from three distant graves in separate glass dishes and arranges them according to her remembered map. Fine strands press against the glass in matching pulses whenever the central sample is touched, planting experimental clue C009 that the patches remain part of one underground system. Arthur Penhaligon appears above the flooded plot and closes the sluice, trapping Marget Halloway below as the loosened ground begins to sink. The numbness spreads across Marget Halloway's left palm.

chapter_plans.title: The Bone Under the Root
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway follows the exposed filaments to the central stone and identifies the embedded bone as Oswin Kerrow's by its dated carving and his damaged-chisel mark — without yet knowing why he lies at the centre.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway follows the white filaments revealed by the collapsed mud and finds that they curve around the buried dead rather than penetrating most of the coffins. Every strand converges beneath the central stone. Using her left hand, Marget Halloway clears the base and recovers the bone fragment first found there, paying off C010. The carved date matches Oswin Kerrow's disappearance, and the cut marks carry the distinctive stagger made by the damaged chisel Oswin Kerrow taught her to use. When Marget Halloway touches the fragment, a concentrated cold surges from the bone into the stone while the surrounding graves briefly warm — Oswin Kerrow does not speak or convey meaning. The physical trail now proves the body's identity and that the network routes through this unmarked plot; what Oswin Kerrow meant by lying there, and what the moss takes, remain unread. Combined with Arthur Penhaligon's flooding and ledger confiscation, the scene reads as active concealment, though his ultimate purpose is still unknown. Arthur Penhaligon arrives carrying a stone maul and orders Marget Halloway away from the exposed root. The numbness crosses Marget Halloway's left wrist, leaving only intermittent pressure in two fingers.

chapter_plans.beat_summary: Continuing beside the exposed rib cage, Marget Halloway prevents Arthur Penhaligon from covering the root and uses the last intermittent pressure in her left fingers to compare an untouched grave, a moss-covered grave, and the central stone. The untouched carving retains the distinct tactile residue by which Marget Halloway reads the dead, while the moss-covered carving has been scraped empty of every human trace. When Marget Halloway cuts the moss, its aggressive regrowth accelerates toward the remaining residue, paying off C003 as feeding behavior rather than ordinary growth. Marget Halloway repeats the sealed-dish experiment beside the exposed root; all samples pulse together, the outer graves lose their residual impressions, and a concentrated current passes through Oswin Kerrow into a buried glass receiver, paying off C009. Following the receiver's tube, Marget Halloway finds Arthur Penhaligon's concealed harvesting apparatus. Arthur Penhaligon draws the luminous condensate into his gloved grip, and a strip of deeply aged skin visible above his cuff smooths within seconds. Combined with the filament convergence and Oswin Kerrow's identified remains from the prior day, Marget Halloway earns the full answer through physical evidence and touch: the fungal network digests the souls held in the graves; Oswin Kerrow deliberately made himself its anchor so it would consume him before reaching the other dead; and Arthur Penhaligon accelerated the decay to harvest the extracted essence for unnatural longevity. Arthur Penhaligon attacks the apparatus rather than explain it, rupturing the receiver and driving the network into a feeding surge. The numbness advances through Marget Halloway's left forearm.

chapter_plans.title: The Last Stone Marget Halloway Can Read
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway discovers that shattering the central stone will collapse the network, chooses to violate her lifelong rule against destroying carved stone, and seizes Arthur Penhaligon's maul.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: The feeding surge pulls black moss through the opened names, forcing Marget Halloway to work with rapidly failing sensation. Marget Halloway blocks one exposed filament with broken slate and observes every connected strand recoil, confirming that the network depends on continuity through the central stone. The raven remains fixed to the tilting central stone even when the slab shifts violently; its wings beat, but its claws cannot leave the carved surface. Combined with the raven's unbroken vigil since Marget Halloway arrived and the network's response to fractures, this visual behavior reveals that the raven is bound to the intact anchor and that the central stone is the network's structural lock. Marget Halloway tests an existing fracture with an iron wedge. The network stops feeding for one heartbeat, the outer graves warm, and the concentrated cold of Oswin Kerrow weakens. Marget Halloway concludes that shattering the stone will kill the network and release the anchor, but Marget Halloway cannot learn whether Oswin Kerrow desires that release. Arthur Penhaligon tries to remove the wedge and preserve the stone. During the struggle, Marget Halloway lets Arthur Penhaligon believe the numb left hand has failed, then uses the weight of the dead right arm to trap the maul shaft and take the weapon. The numbness reaches Marget Halloway's left elbow, and the final pressure in the left fingertips disappears. Marget Halloway raises the maul over the carved face, crossing the boundary Marget Halloway has obeyed throughout her life.

chapter_plans.title: The Blow Marget Halloway Cannot Feel
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Marget Halloway shatters the central stone, frees Oswin Kerrow and destroys the network, while Arthur Penhaligon escapes with his marked hands exposed and Marget Halloway leaves unable to feel stone ever again.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Marget Halloway begins the downward swing, but Arthur Penhaligon catches the shaft and the maul glances from the central fracture. During the struggle, the gloves Arthur Penhaligon has never removed tear free, paying off C008: both hands are mapped with black root scars, old puncture sites, and alternating bands of withered and unnaturally renewed skin that physically expose years of repeated harvesting. The broken receiver has left Arthur Penhaligon's hands rapidly aging, yet Arthur Penhaligon abandons Marget Halloway rather than remain when the stone begins to fail. Marget Halloway braces the maul without feeling the grip, aligns the head by sight, and strikes the central stone with iron. The stone breaks through Oswin Kerrow's carved chisel line. Every filament contracts, the moss turns grey, the graveyard rises as the sinking network collapses, and the concentrated cold of Oswin Kerrow vanishes. The raven's claws finally release, paying off C006, but the central stone falls into fragments and leaves the raven circling over empty ground with nowhere to land. The complete loss of touch that began with Marget Halloway's first readings pays off C008's personal dimension as well: Marget Halloway cannot feel the maul, the shattered slate, blood from damaged calluses, or the last cold of Oswin Kerrow. Arthur Penhaligon escapes across the moor with visibly marked hands and a remaining trace of harvested essence, preserving the wider threat while ending the graveyard scheme. Marget Halloway logs total bilateral hand numbness by watching the pen move rather than feeling it, then walks out across ground Marget Halloway can no longer read.
